title: Syntax: Program Structure, Blocks, and Comments
description: How each language structures a program, delimits blocks, and handles comments and naming.
objectives: Compare program structure across the three languages
Compare comment syntax and naming conventions

content.heading: Python
content.body: A Python file has no required top-level structure — statements at module level just run in order. Blocks are defined by indentation (no braces), and a colon introduces a new indented block (after if, for, def, class, etc.). Comments use #. Naming convention: snake_case for variables/functions, PascalCase for classes.

content.heading: Java
content.body: Every piece of Java code must live inside a class; a runnable program needs a public static void main(String[] args) method as its entry point. Blocks are delimited by curly braces {}, and every statement ends with a semicolon. Comments use //, /* */, and /** */ (Javadoc). Naming convention: camelCase for methods/variables, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants.

content.heading: C
content.body: A C program needs an int main() function as its entry point, but code can exist at file scope outside any function (global variables, other function definitions) — there's no requirement everything live inside a class. Blocks use curly braces {}, statements end with semicolons, and #include/#define preprocessor directives (starting with #) are processed before real compilation. Comments use // (C99+) and /* */. Naming convention is less strictly enforced by tooling than Java's, but snake_case is common.

content.explanation: The same conditional in each language: Python relies purely on indentation and a colon; Java and C both require parentheses around the condition and braces around the block.

content.heading: Key Differences
content.body: The most visible structural difference is block delimitation: Python uses indentation as syntax (inconsistent indentation is a real error), while Java and C use braces (indentation is just a readability convention, not enforced by the compiler). Java requires all code inside a class; C and Python both allow top-level functions/statements outside any class-like construct.

content.heading: When It Matters
content.body: Coming from Java or C to Python, forgetting that indentation is meaningful (not cosmetic) is the most common early stumbling block. Coming from Python to Java or C, forgetting closing braces or semicolons is the mirror-image mistake.

keyPoints: Python uses indentation to define blocks; Java and C use braces
Java requires all code inside a class; Python and C allow top-level code/functions
Comment styles and naming conventions differ, but // and /* */ are shared by Java and C
